subject: german

rounds.lie: “Ich habe ein Praktikum gemacht” means “I did a practical exam”.
rounds.why: Wrong: “das Praktikum” is a “work placement/internship”, not a practical exam (“die praktische Prüfung”).
rounds.truth: “Ich habe ein Praktikum gemacht” means “I did a work placement”.

rounds.lie: “Das Gymnasium beginnt um acht Uhr” means “The gym opens at eight o'clock”.
rounds.why: False friend: “das Gymnasium” is a “grammar school”, not a gym. A gym is “die Turnhalle”.
rounds.truth: “Das Gymnasium beginnt um acht Uhr” means “The grammar school starts at eight o'clock”.
truths: “eine Prüfung bestehen” means “to pass an exam”.

rounds.why: “Die Arbeitslosigkeit” means “unemployment”. A workplace is “der Arbeitsplatz”.
truths: “Ich möchte Krankenpfleger werden” means “I would like to become a nurse”.
“Ich kann mich auf ihn verlassen” means “I can rely on him”.

rounds.lie: At school, “die Note” means “a short note/message”.
rounds.why: False friend — “die Note” means “a grade/mark”. A note/message is “die Notiz / die Nachricht”.
truths: “Eine Prüfung bestehen” means “to pass an exam”.

rounds.lie: “Später möchte ich Tierärztin werden” means “Later I am becoming a vet right now”.
rounds.why: Wrong: “später … werden” expresses a future wish — “later I would like to become a vet”. “bekommen” (to get) is not used here.
rounds.truth: “Später möchte ich Tierärztin werden” means “Later I would like to become a vet”.
truths: “eine Stelle suchen” means “to look for a job”.

rounds.lie: “Der Chef war freundlich” means “The chef (cook) was friendly”.
rounds.why: False friend: “der Chef” means “the boss”, not a cook. A cook is “der Koch”.
rounds.truth: “Der Chef war freundlich” means “The boss was friendly”.

rounds.lie: “Ich habe eine gute Note bekommen” means “I received a nice short note”.
rounds.why: False friend: “die Note” here means a school “grade/mark”, and “bekommen” means “to get/receive”.
rounds.truth: “Ich habe eine gute Note bekommen” means “I got a good grade”.
